title: SRI-PART-C4 — A match on category shows the FULL value on the row
custom_preconds:
WHY THIS MATTERS TO A REAL USER
a broad hunt for "brakes"

BEFORE YOU START
A part carrying a distinctive value in category — a value that appears in NO other field of that record.

NOTE: proven to match on category (word)

TYPE THIS INTO THE SEARCH BOX — exactly as written:
.Brake Parts
custom_steps:
1. Open search and type the term.
2. Open the Parts tab.
3. Find the record. Without opening it, read the SECOND line of the row.
4. It should carry a labelled note naming the field that matched.
5. Now check the value in that note against the record itself.
custom_expected:
The second line carries a labelled note — such as "Contact match: ...", "Matched: ...", "Unit: ...", "VIN: ..." — naming what matched, with the part you typed highlighted inside it.

THE THING TO CHECK IS WHETHER THE VALUE IS COMPLETE. The note must show the WHOLE category value, not just the characters you typed. Open the record and compare. If you typed part of a longer value and the note shows only that part, this is a FAIL — it is SV-10619 and SV-10551, and it means two different records can draw identically.

---
SOURCE — quoted verbatim from PRD v1.5, section 5.3:
"Every row has a left-side entity icon, a primary line (bold), a secondary line (subdued), and an optional right-side cluster (status badges, counts, and quick-action buttons on hover). The matched substring of the query is highlighted in the primary and secondary text — searching `Fib` highlights "Fib" in "S1-644 Fibridge Commercial"."

This case's expected result is the source's own sentence, unchanged (Rule 113). The plain-language wording above is our restatement, added after the quote; where the two could be read as disagreeing, the quote wins.
